gaps.what: When Buddu was captured: the Buddu page has Kabaka Jjunju (r. 1780-1797) with no year, the Buganda page 'Junju (c.1790-1800)'. The gain stays at the 1800 placeholder (confidence 1) to match kingdom-of-bunyoro's 1800 loss.

The 17th-18th-century growth from the first state (17 cells) to the whole region is one confidence-1 gain at 1800 (80 cells, counterpart nobody); no page dates a county. Busoga: the Buganda page says 'parts of Busoga' conquered, the Busoga page 'unable to conquer Busoga'; 9 Busoga cells stay in the shape, flagged.
The founding stays 1300 at confidence 1: the Kato Kintu page has 'fl. Late 13th century' (infobox) against 'early fourteenth century' (table) and no year for the founding of Buganda.
When the tribute of Kooki ended: vassal_end set to June 1894 (end of the kingdom) at confidence 1; the Kooki page has the incorporation into Buganda on 18 November 1896, after the dossier ends.
Mubende, Nakasongola and Kiboga: kept with Bunyoro by cutting them from Buganda's 1800 shape; when and how they passed to Buganda (and the Uganda Agreement counties of 1900) is not on any page read.

Not in this repair list and untouched: (a) its 1800 loss of Masaka and Rakai should be split like Buganda's (Buddu a loss; Kooki broke away c. 1740 per the Kooki page, so not Bunyoro's in 1800); (b) its 1830 keyframe drops Mubende, Nakasongola, Kiboga and Kyankwanzi (34 cells in all) with no event, so they become nobody's land after 1830.
